llama1B-ORPO.alt: A terminal where the same two prompts, a two-sentence explanation of recursion and a two-line reply declining a meeting, are sent to the base Llama 3.2 1B and to the ORPO fine-tuned model through Ollama, and each answers in turn.
llama1B-ORPO.caption: The ORPO fine-tuned Llama 3.2 1B, served by Ollama from the exported GGUF, answers differently from the base model: here it drops the preamble and the placeholder.
llama1B-ORPO.source: Retrained on 18 November 2026 with the repo's notebook recipe (Unsloth, Llama 3.2 1B Instruct in 4-bit, LoRA r=16, ORPO beta 0.1, lr 5e-6, 200 steps of batch 2 x 4 on 5000 UltraFeedback pairs; nothing cut, run on an RTX 4060 instead of a Colab T4; changes: TRL 1.15 API names and fp16 forced as on the T4). Merged to 16-bit, exported to an F16 GGUF with llama.cpp's converter (Unsloth's own GGUF step was replaced), created in Ollama under a scratch name and removed afterwards. The base model went through the same F16 GGUF path. Greedy decoding with a fixed seed. The effect is small: the training log shows the preference margin barely moving (reward accuracy about 0.5 to 0.6), and both models still answer wrongly when asked what ORPO is. Recorded on two prompts the model never trained on, answers shown as generated.

computational_Perception_Jupyter_Noteboo.alt: A browser page showing twelve test photos of flowers one by one, each with the predicted species and its probability, the top three species as bars, and the true species in a green box when right and a red box when wrong.
computational_Perception_Jupyter_Noteboo.caption: The ResNet fine-tuned in the FGIC notebook names flower species in held-out photos, and the page shows the daisy it mistook for another.
computational_Perception_Jupyter_Noteboo.source: Retrained on 18 November 2026 with the notebook TL09_FGIC.ipynb's final recipe (KerasHub resnet_vd_50_ssld_v2_imagenet, whole network unfrozen, flip, brightness, contrast and crop augmentation, Adam 5e-5, ReduceLROnPlateau and early stopping on validation accuracy, up to 50 epochs; nothing cut, stopped after 30 epochs by early stopping). Test accuracy 86.7% on the 6149-image Oxford 102 Flowers test split (the notebook reports 86.29%). Recorded on a local demo page backed by a Python endpoint running the model; 12 random test photos, 10 right and 2 wrong. Confidences are often low because the model spreads probability over 102 species, even when right.

transfer-learning-llm-vision.alt: A terminal where three held-out cardiology questions are put to Llama 3.1 8B with its LoRA adapter switched off and then on, each answer streaming in: the base model rambles into multiple-choice options, the fine-tuned one gives a compact numbered clinical answer.
transfer-learning-llm-vision.caption: After the CardioLLM QLoRA fine-tune, Llama 3.1 8B answers cardiology questions in the trained format instead of drifting into quiz options.
transfer-learning-llm-vision.source: Retrained on 18 November 2026 with CardioLLM_Finetuning.ipynb's recipe (Unsloth, Llama 3.1 8B in 4-bit, QLoRA r=16, the notebook's 11 cardiology examples, 80 steps at batch 2 x 4, lr 2e-4, bf16; nothing cut, Llama 3.1 8B fit in 8 GB, training took about 4.5 minutes; only TRL 1.15 argument names changed). Recorded live: one process loads the model once and answers three questions that are not in the training data with the adapter off (base) and on (fine-tuned), sampled at temperature 0.7 with a fixed seed and cut at 100 new tokens. The fine-tuned answers copy the style of 11 training examples and contain medical inaccuracies, so this shows a style shift, not reliable medicine.

vgg11-cifar10-transfer-learning.alt: A browser page showing ten enlarged 32x32 CIFAR-10 test images one by one, each with the predicted class and probability, the top three classes as bars, and the true class in a green box when right and a red box when wrong.
vgg11-cifar10-transfer-learning.caption: The retrained VGG11 classifies held-out CIFAR-10 images and the page shows a cat it mistook for a dog.
vgg11-cifar10-transfer-learning.source: Retrained on 18 November 2026 with the repo's notebook recipe (VGG11 with batch norm, ImageNet weights, 224 px, same augmentation, 90/10 split, discriminative learning rates, 5 epochs, best validation loss kept). Changes: fp16 mixed precision and batches of 64 accumulated in pairs to fit 8 GB, learning-rate finder skipped (the notebook hardcodes 5e-4), CIFAR-10 read from the HuggingFace mirror of the same official split. Test accuracy 92.6% on the 10000 CIFAR-10 test images. Recorded on a local demo page backed by a Python endpoint running the model; 10 random test images, 9 right and 1 wrong, matching the error rate. The endpoint ran on CPU.

Oxford-IIIT_Pet_Dataset-Classification.alt: A browser page showing twelve test photos of cats and dogs one by one, each with the predicted breed and its probability, the top three breeds as bars, and the true breed in a green box when right and a red box when wrong.
Oxford-IIIT_Pet_Dataset-Classification.caption: The retrained MobileNetV2 names the breed of held-out pet photos and the page shows the one it got wrong.
Oxford-IIIT_Pet_Dataset-Classification.source: Retrained on 18 November 2026 with the repo's notebook recipe (MobileNetV2 on ImageNet weights, frozen-base phase then fine-tuning phase, same head, callbacks and learning rates, 20 epochs run in total; nothing cut). Test accuracy 90.1% on the 3669-image Oxford-IIIT Pet test split, which, as in the notebook, also served as validation for early stopping. Recorded on a local demo page backed by a Python endpoint running the model; 12 random test photos, 11 right and 1 wrong, matching the error rate. The endpoint ran on CPU.

GTZAN-Classification.alt: A browser page showing, one at a time, the colourful mel spectrogram of twelve 4-second music clips with their file names, the predicted genre with probability bars, and the true genre in a green box when right and a red box when wrong.
GTZAN-Classification.caption: The retrained CNN names the genre of held-out song clips from their spectrograms, and the page shows the pop and rock clips it got wrong.
GTZAN-Classification.source: Retrained on 18 November 2026 with the repo's notebook recipe (4 s chunks with 2 s overlap, mel spectrogram resized to 150x150, the same five-block CNN, Adam 1e-4, batch 32, 20 epochs; nothing cut). One change: the 80/20 split is by song instead of by chunk, because the notebook's chunk-level split puts overlapping pieces of the same song in both sets, so its 89% is inflated (the unchanged chunk-level split reproduces it: 88.9% here). Test accuracy 74.6% on the 2998 chunks of 200 held-out songs (74% on each song's first 4 s clip, 83% when a song's chunks are averaged); GTZAN read from the HuggingFace mirror marsyas/gtzan, the known corrupt jazz.00054 file skipped. Recorded on a local demo page backed by a Python endpoint running the model; 12 random held-out clips, 9 right and 3 wrong, matching the error rate. The clip is shown as its spectrogram, as the video is silent.

MNIST-Classification.alt: A browser page where a mouse draws the digits 3, 4, 7, 2, 9 and 5 one after another on a black canvas while bars for 0 to 9 show the network's live probabilities and a large predicted digit.
MNIST-Classification.caption: The NumPy network, running in the browser, recognises digits drawn by hand that it never trained on.
MNIST-Classification.source: Retrained on 18 November 2026 with the repo's notebook recipe (784-10-10 NumPy network, Nesterov momentum, 500 iterations, same hyperparameters; only changes: fixed seed and accuracy measured on the 1000 held-out rows, since the notebook's last cell scores the training set). Test accuracy 93.7% on 1000 held-out Kaggle train.csv rows. Recorded on a local demo page that runs the exported weights in JavaScript; six hand-drawn digits, all read correctly.

algor-tmica.alt: A terminal: the Wikipedia search engine indexes its 100 collection, counts 51 results for a boolean AND query and 8 for an AND NOT query, finds none for the misspelled word 'pythn', then finds 59 with spelling correction and lists real article titles such as Python and Aprendizaje automatico.
algor-tmica.caption: An inverted-index search engine answers boolean queries over Wikipedia articles and recovers from misspellings with edit distance.
algor-tmica.source: Recorded 18 November 2026 in a real terminal (termrec) from a fresh clone, numpy in a venv; the repo's own searcher only prints internal ids (its snippet mode is not implemented), so titles are printed by a 10-line helper that calls the repo's SAR_Indexer class.
